source.quote: With Kelp'thar completed, it does give us a chance to look around at some of the farms. And from the quest mobs, I think we might have a couple. Because although we don't have herbalism, we do have skinning. So, let's put it to use. Plus, our first couple of hours of exploring the zone, checking out some spawns and doing quests has actually netted us 1,000 raw gold. Not bad. So, skinning. Down around the Legion's Pass, the first quest area with the sunken ship, we have two primary types of skinnable mobs here. The first ones are these crabs, the split claw skitters. They're neutral and spawn in a pretty wide area, and when skinned, they drop Cataclysm leather, savage leather. We technically already had access to this resource in Zul'Drak Vale from the heroic Zul'Gurub dungeon, which is a Cataclysm dungeon, but here, with skinning as one of our two professions, it very well may be a main source of income, which isn't bad because it does have a market value of around 7 to 10 gold each. Plus, when skinning these kind of mobs down here, we do have a chance to gain the strange bloated stomach, which essentially is a loot box of one to three volatiles. We can get air, fire, water, or earth, but we really want to see water or at least fire, which have price tags around 15 to 30 gold each compared to earth and air that are closer to three to five gold.

So, when at all possible, I want to make sure to capitalize on these eels and then farm the crabs while the eels are spawning. The route I'm taking looks more or less like this because while these underwater beasts aren't on a super tight hyper spawn, they do seem to have a general four spawn over this area, so as long as the loop is wide enough, they keep spawning. source.file: 032 - From 0 Gold To a WoW Token, But I Can ONLY Farm Vashj'ir ｜ Goldbound Ep. 31.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/032 - From 0 Gold To a WoW Token, But I Can ONLY Farm Vashj'ir ｜ Goldbound Ep. 31.en-orig.txt
source.quote: So, the spot is in the Shimmering Expanse and around the SilverTide Hollow, down on the ground in the SilverTide Trench. Around here, we have a few more crabs, the green sand crabs, as well as some more eels, the spike-tooth eels. And these guys have all the same loot on their skinning tables as our Kelp'thar farm. The only difference, they are more densely packed and aren't surrounded by non-skinnable mobs. Plus, doing circles around the Hollow does result in a pretty good loot per farming. The cherry on top though, well, the ledge that we farm on is actually overlooking the spawn location for none other than Mobus. Oh, yeah. So, every hour that we spend skinning here, we're not only getting consistent gold from trade goods, but we're also camping Mobus, and we will definitely get a few extra kills on him.

source.file: 032 - From 0 Gold To a WoW Token, But I Can ONLY Farm Vashj'ir ｜ Goldbound Ep. 31.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/032 - From 0 Gold To a WoW Token, But I Can ONLY Farm Vashj'ir ｜ Goldbound Ep. 31.en-orig.txt
source.quote: So, I think I know what I have to do. It's fishing time. And it might be surprising that we're this far into a completely underwater zone before we even talking about fishing, but it's for a bit of a reason. Because although I sometimes sport my Darkmoon Faire water hat for style, it isn't currently Darkmoon Faire week, so I can't access the pools from it. Plus, while swimming underwater, we can't technically fish. So, there's only a few locations that you can actually even cast a rod in Vashj'ir. One of them is outside of Throne of the Tides in this underwater area. is up on top of some of the mountains that peak out over the water. This one is an interesting part of the zone, but other than fishable water, it's not home to much else. And lastly, within the quest hub caves that we hang out in. The downside, there are zero fishing pools in Vashj'ir, at least that I've seen. And I've looked around quite a bit and I have track fish on. So, that means that we have to stick to open water fishing and the fish in these waters, well, let's just say they may only be giving Elwynn Forest a run for its money. Standing here and fishing, the gold per hour is a whopping 38 gold per hour. And with our current status towards the token, it isn't something I can really spend too much time on here.

source.file: 032 - From 0 Gold To a WoW Token, But I Can ONLY Farm Vashj'ir ｜ Goldbound Ep. 31.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/032 - From 0 Gold To a WoW Token, But I Can ONLY Farm Vashj'ir ｜ Goldbound Ep. 31.en-orig.txt
source.quote: But, that doesn't mean that Vashj'ir fish can't be profitable. In the quest hubs, we do have some vendors that sell some fish. Depending on the market, some of these dishes can spike in value because they are used by some players to get certain completeness achievements in the game. I think most of these are used for cooking ones or collection logs from having eaten them. And things like this simmered squid can fetch a fair price. As you can see here, I've already sold a few for 10 to 500 gold. They don't actually sell in bulk. It's just going to be one or two here and there, but it seems to be the best we can do for the fish for the time being. And while there are some cool oddities still here in Vashj'ir, like the sunken vicro who actually have some Wrath of the Lich King materials on their tables, or the vast and empty lands of the Abyssal Reef, I think I found most of the gold farms that are actually going to move the needle here. And right now, my route is pretty set. I can farm leather while overlooking the mob spawn, and once I tag him, I have about 3 hours before he should spawn again. And during those 3 hours, I can do loot checks for another Poseidus spawn, and then head over for some pickpocketing on the Naga farm. In between sessions of this, I can also drop down into Throne of the Tides for some raw gold, but we're currently about 5 days into this year with only 2 days left to farm the token within the first week. So, if we want to do it within the first 7 days, we really have to lock in. But with that in mind, we have a bit of an interesting dilemma going into the weekend because we have 2 days left, and realistically about 20 to 25 hours that I could grind, and 20 hours on skinning farms is really only going to net 80 to 100,000 gold, at least at these rates.

source.quote: And I'm saying hopefully because so far I've had the Decimator listed for about 20 hours, but still no bites. So, after only 1,400 junk boxes and about 10,000 pickpockets, I can rest. Even though that was 9 to 11 hours of pickpocketing, it's actually crazy that we got both weapons. The luck on that is insane. Let's just hope the luck continues with some sales. It's officially the morning of day seven on this challenge, and after all that pickpocketing and a lot of luck, we are now in a position where if one of the swords has sold, well, we would have enough for a token to leave this watery zone right now. So, let's check. Well, that doesn't look like any sales on the sword, and that does mean that the seven-day aspect of this challenge has failed. But, that does mean I can pop back in briefly to the older zones just to train mining and herbalism, and then come back to test out dual gathering. I mean, to be fair, I was going to do this even if we just got the token, because of course for a gold bound, we have to test dual gathering. So, here we go. The Bashir dual gather test. My plan is to basically do hours and hours of dual gathering either until we earn enough gold from trade goods or until one of the weapons sells. The route I'm taking here for dual gathering though is pretty simple, and it's really just flying over all the spawn points for Posidus to try to tag him again, which uh I did. But, this time, since we have some massive values on the auction house, I'm actually just going to learn him and add it to the collection log for Goldie. And as far as materials for dual gathering, we're mostly just pulling in stormvine and Ashara's veils for herbs.

records.summary: Twilights Blade sold for over 350,000 g; Krol the Decapitator for just under 200,000 g. The 553,000 g mailbox included other goods, and the total cash stack reached 615,000 g. These were sales from an exceptionally lucky pickpocket session, not a normal hourly farming return.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/032 - From 0 Gold To a WoW Token, But I Can ONLY Farm Vashj'ir ｜ Goldbound Ep. 31.en-orig.txt
source.quote: So, for today, I'll just keep dual gathering, and after a few hours, we can check back to see if the auction sold. And the verdict? Oh ho. Oh, yeah. Although these went for way below market value, the value is still absolutely insane. Over 350,000 gold for the Twilight Blade, which to whoever sniped that, I am wishing them luck on flipping it to two to three million. That would be good value for them for sure. And the Cruel Decapitator as well, sold for just under 200k. All in all, the biggest mailbox we've seen so far at 553,000 gold into the bags, which gives us a full cash stack of 615k. And of course, that's enough for the Vashj'ir token. There we go. But travelers, it doesn't end there. Because now we have 315,000 gold surplus, plus about 220k from Wetlands still hiding in the bank, which we can now return to.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/032 - From 0 Gold To a WoW Token, But I Can ONLY Farm Vashj'ir ｜ Goldbound Ep. 31.en-orig.txt
source.quote: So, here's my plan. I'm going to go ahead and invest 100,000 of this right now into an additional warband bank tab, increasing our total bank storage and farmable space. And then, the extra 250k from Vashj'ir, I'm actually going to put away in the warband bank just to save up for the next bank tab of 500k. If we get another massive sale during the zone, we can use some of these savings to buy the next tab as well. I think the final tab after this is something crazy like 2.5 mil, so a long ways to go for sure, but these extra tabs will come in super handy for stockpiling extra trade goods or junk boxes. All right. So, here we are. Exactly back where we left off about a week ago in the Wetlands with 220,000 gold in the bags. And travelers, well, I'm not done quite yet today, cuz I feel we've pretty fully explored Wetlands. So, let's take our best farm, the skinning hyper spawn farm, and just sit here and list auctions until we have a token. Which the timing on this is actually working out quite well. Our cash stack is rising and the wild token is falling a little bit today. So, after a few hours of farming, well, with a little help of raw gold at the end, of course, boom, another token. This one is the token to escape Wetlands and roll a new zone. So, let's do it. For our next zones, we still have all the old options of Edwin pass, home to Karazhan, and still the longest standing zone that hasn't been rolled, Badlands, of course, which we are familiar with. Then the two new zones opened by Wetlands, Twilight Highlands and Arathi Highlands. Of course, the two Kalimdor zones accessible by boat, the Barrens and Dustwallow Marsh, courtesy of Wetlands. So, all in all, there is six potential zones to spin and let's waste no time on it. And see where we're going next episode.
